questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t-9{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t-9{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=-2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =(1)^{2}-3(1)^{3}+C \\ -2 & =1-3+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =(2)^{2}-3(2)^{3} \\  & =4-24 \\  & =-20\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $20\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-6{e}^{-2t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-6{e}^{-2t})\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2t})+C \\  & =3{e}^{-2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =3{e}^{0}+C \\ 2 & =3+C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3{e}^{-2t}-1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (12{t}^{3}+20t)\text{d}t \\  & =3{t}^{4}+10{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=25.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}25 & =3({1}^{4})+10({1}^{2})+C \\ 25 & =13+C \\ C & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3{t}^{4}+10{t}^{2}+12.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time.

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 6\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(\pi )=10.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+C \\ 10 & =-6(-1)+C \\ 10 & =6+C \\ C & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+4.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{6}{{t}^{2}}-3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{6}{{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t+\int (-3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{6}{t}-3t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-\frac{6}{2}-3(2)+C \\ 1 & =-9+C \\ C & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-\frac{6}{t}-3t+10.$
